# Cipherlink

> An end-to-end encrypted one-time secret-sharing service that uses a
> capability URL as the credential. The browser generates a random key,
> encrypts the secret with NaCl secretbox, and embeds the key in the URL
> fragment so the server never sees it.

Cipherlink is a small, auditable demonstration of how to build a
secret-sharing tool where the server is honest-but-curious. It is
designed to be readable end-to-end in a single sitting (~600 LOC).

## Design in one sentence

A 32-byte symmetric key is generated client-side, the secret is encrypted
with `nacl.secretbox`, only the ciphertext + nonce + an unguessable id is
posted to the server, and the key travels in the URL fragment (`#k=…`)
which browsers never send in HTTP requests.

## Documentation

- [README.md](README.md): Quickstart, API surface, trust model, license.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): Threat model, primitive choice, intentional
  non-goals (no DELETE, no list, no edit, no read receipts).
- [.repobility/access.yml](.repobility/access.yml): Endpoint-by-endpoint
  authorization matrix documenting the capability-URL model.

## Source files

- `server.js`: Express + an in-memory store with TTL and read-count limits.
  Validates wire shapes, atomically consumes reads, sweeps expired records.
- `public/crypto-utils.js`: NaCl secretbox wrapper — keygen, encrypt,
  decrypt, base64url helpers.
- `public/app.js`: Compose flow — encrypt, POST, build URL with fragment key.
- `public/view.js`: Viewer flow — peek meta, confirm, consume + decrypt.
- `public/index.html` / `public/view.html`: Strict-CSP SPA shells.
- `tests/`: Node native test runner suites — crypto roundtrip, server
  validation + one-time-read property, capability-URL authorization invariants.

## How to run

    npm install
    npm start
    # open http://127.0.0.1:3000
